requested_parts: Number of Escape Pods selected in a four-player game.
How the selected Pods are distributed between Sections A and B.
The starting orientation of the Pods.
The exact tokens initially placed in the Intruder bag.
answers.answer: 1. Select 3 Escape Pod tokens for four players. 2. Put the lowest-numbered Pod in Section A, the next-numbered in Section B, then alternate A/B (so the third goes in A). 3. All Pods start Locked side up. 4. Put 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, and 3 Adults plus 1 additional Adult per player in the bag. At four players that is 7 Adults, 14 tokens total.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Setup states: “Take randomly chosen Escape Pod tokens: 2 pods for 1–2 players, 3 for 3–4 players, 4 for 5 players. Place the lowest-numbered pod in Section "A", the next (in numerical order) in Section "B", then alternate A/B. All pods start with their Locked side face up. Return the rest to the box.” 4. Setup states: “Put these Intruder tokens in the Intruder bag: 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player. Place the remaining Intruder tokens and the Intruder Carcass tokens next to the board.” Inference: four players therefore means 3 + 4 = 7 Adult tokens and 1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 7 = 14 tokens in total.

requested_parts: How Objectives are filtered by player count.
How many of each type are dealt and their secrecy.
When players choose between their Objectives and what happens to the rejected card.
Whether Eggs trigger the choice.
answers.answer: 1. Let P equal the actual player count and remove from both the Corporate and Personal decks every Objective requiring more than P players. 2. Shuffle the decks separately and deal each player one Corporate and one Personal Objective, kept hidden. 3. Players do not choose one during the initial deal: when the first Intruder miniature of any type appears on the board, every player immediately chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other from the game face down; nobody may look at another player's removed Objective. 4. Eggs are not Intruders, so they do not trigger that choice.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Setup says: “Let P be the actual number of players in this game. Remove from both Objective decks (Corporate and Personal) every card requiring more than P players. Shuffle the two decks separately and deal each player 1 Corporate and 1 Personal Objective card, kept hidden. (You receive Objectives before the Character draft on purpose — pick a Character suited to your Objective.)” 3–4. Critical gameplay moments says: “First Encounter: the first time an Intruder miniature (of any type) appears on the board, every player immediately chooses 1 of their 2 Objective cards and removes the other from the game face down (unseen by anyone — players may never look at others' removed Objectives). Then the triggering Encounter is resolved. Eggs are not Intruders and do not trigger this.”

requested_parts: The cards discarded to pay for an Action card with printed cost 2 in the stated hand scenario.
Whether Contamination cards can substitute for Action-card payment.
How to handle an Action card with OR effects.
answers.answer: 1. Discard the played Action card itself plus the two other Action cards to pay its printed cost of 2; that is 3 Action cards total. The two Contamination cards are not used as payment. 2. Contamination cards cannot replace any Action cards in the payment. 3. If the card has two sections separated by OR, choose one section/effect; the played card and its printed-cost payment still apply.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Action Cost says: “For an Action card, also discard the card you play: printed cost n requires n + 1 Action cards in total.” It also says: “Contamination cards are not Action cards: they can never be discarded to pay any Action cost.” The example states: “Captain's Basic Repairs has an extra cost of 2. Discard Basic Repairs itself + 2 other Action cards = 3 Action cards total. Those three cards are sufficient for its printed Action-card payment; Contamination cannot replace any of them.” Inference: the stated cost-2 card plus the two other Action cards satisfy the payment exactly. 3. The Action-card rules say: “To use one, discard that card face up and pay its cost by discarding the required number of additional Action cards. If a card has two sections separated by "OR," choose one.”

requested_parts: When the Character suffers Fire damage after taking one Action and passing.
Whether the Character may take normal Actions again this Player Phase.
Whether cards may be discarded on passing.
Whether later players' rounds cause additional Fire wounds to this passed Character.
answers.answer: 1. The Character takes 1 Light Wound at the end of their own passing round, after declaring Pass. 2. They cannot take further normal Actions for the rest of this Player Phase, though the general rule allows an Interruption card after passing subject to its requirements. 3. At the moment of passing, they may discard any number of cards from their hand. 4. No: later players' rounds do not give a passed Character further Fire wounds that turn; Fire is checked at the end of that Character's own round.
answers.evidence: 1, 4. Turn Structure says: “A Character who ends their round in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Light Wound (every round; only after finishing their own round — passing players take it once at the end of their round and no more that turn).” The passing table says: “Fire in your Room | Take 1 Light Wound at the end of your own passing round. Later players' rounds do not give you further Fire wounds that turn.” FAQ says: “Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.” 2. The passing table says: “Normal Actions | You cannot take further normal Actions; Interruption remains permitted as below.” It also says: “You may still play Interruption after passing, subject to its usual card requirements (FAQ Rules 21).” 3. The passing table says: “At the moment you pass, you may discard any number of cards from your hand.”

requested_parts: What happens to an unexplored Room tile and its Item Counter on entry.
How its Exploration effect and token are resolved.
When and where the ordinary Movement Noise roll occurs, and how Silence/Danger affect it.
What happens to a Noise marker when its Corridor already has one.
How an already occupied destination affects the Movement Noise roll.
answers.answer: 1. On entering a face-down Room, flip the tile face up and reveal its Exploration token. The token's number sets the Item Counter for ordinary Rooms by rotating the tile until that number faces the board's Item Counter symbol; the Nest and Room Covered With Slime have no Item count. 2. Resolve the revealed effect, then remove the Exploration token from the game into the box. A Door effect places a Door token in the Corridor used to enter. 3. After exploration, make the ordinary Noise roll only if the destination has no Character or Intruder; the resulting number places a Noise marker in the corresponding connected Corridor (including a Technical Corridors Entrance if applicable). A Silence Exploration result replaces the Noise roll with no effect (unless the mover has Slime, when it resolves as Danger). A Danger result replaces the roll and moves all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination; if none are eligible, place Noise markers in each connected Corridor lacking one (including Technical Corridors if there is an Entrance). 4. If the numbered Corridor already has a Noise marker, resolve an Encounter instead of placing a second marker there. 5. If any Character or Intruder is already in the destination, do not roll Movement Noise.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Movement rules state: “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box; (2) apply the Movement Noise rule.” Exploration tokens state: “The token's front shows (1) a number = the amount of Items obtainable in that Room, and (2) a special effect symbol.” And: “the Nest and Room Covered With Slime get no Item count. For other Room tiles, rotate the tile until the Exploration token's number faces the Item Counter symbol printed on the board next to the slot.” Doors effect: “place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.” Token handling: “After resolving an Exploration token, remove it from the game into the box; it does not return to a supply or stay on the Room (each is resolved only once, on first entry).” 3. Movement rules state: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward. Otherwise, perform the ordinary Noise roll if the destination is empty (no Characters, no Intruders). If anyone — Character or Intruder — is already there, do NOT roll for Movement Noise.” Exploration effects state: “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.” “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” 4. Noise rules state: “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” 5. Noise rules state: “Remember: never roll for Noise when moving into a Room containing another Character or an Intruder.”

requested_parts: Careful Movement's Action-card cost.
What Careful Movement replaces and where it places Noise.
When Careful Movement is forbidden, including destination Corridor availability.
Whether it can cross Closed Doors and whether a miniature can stop in a Corridor.
answers.answer: 1. Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards. 2. It follows normal Movement restrictions but replaces the post-move Noise roll with placing one Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room entered. It also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with that chosen Noise placement. 3. It cannot be used in Combat or if every Corridor connected to the destination already has a Noise marker. 4. No: Closed Doors block passage for player Movement, including Careful Movement; a miniature can never stop in a Corridor, only in a Room.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Basic Actions says: “Careful Movement (cost 2) — follows normal Movement restrictions, including Closed Doors blocking passage; but instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter. You cannot Carefully Move if all Corridors connected to the destination already hold Noise markers, and you cannot use it while in Combat. The FAQ clarifies that Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.” 4. Movement rules state: “Characters and Intruders may only occupy Rooms (Special Rooms — Hibernatorium, Cockpit, Engines — count as Rooms; Escape Pod tokens are the only exception for Characters). Corridors connect Rooms; no one may ever stop in a Corridor.” Also: “A Closed Door blocks the "neighboring" status for players' Movement.”

requested_parts: What happens when a Noise roll calls for a Corridor that already has Noise.
Which connected Noise markers are removed and when.
How the Encounter draws and handles its token, including Blank versus non-Blank destinations.
How Surprise Attack is determined and whether Contamination cards count.
answers.answer: 1. Since a Corridor cannot hold a second Noise marker, the attempted placement triggers an Encounter. 2. At the start of the Encounter, discard all Noise markers from Corridors connected to the Character's Room, including the Technical Corridors space because this Room has an Entrance. 3. Draw one Intruder token. If it is non-Blank, keep it aside outside the bag and place its matching miniature in the Room; it remains aside unless a rule returns it, such as that Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors. If it is Blank, instead place Noise in every Corridor connected to the Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without an Intruder appearing. 4. For a non-Blank token, compare its number with the number of cards in the triggering player's hand: fewer cards than that number causes a Surprise Attack. Action and Contamination cards both count, so the two Contamination cards in hand contribute to the comparison.
answers.evidence: 1. Noise rules state: “A Corridor may never hold more than 1 Noise marker — if instructed to place a marker where one already is, resolve an Encounter instead.” 2–3. Encounter rules state: “Discard ALL Noise markers from all Corridors connected to the Room (including Technical Corridors if there's an Entrance).” They continue: “Draw 1 Intruder token from the bag (symbol on one side, number on the other). Keep a non-Blank token aside outside the bag; it is not immediately returned. A Blank follows its separate return procedure below.” “Place the matching Intruder miniature in the Room.” “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” Technical Corridors rules state: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board.” 4. Encounter rules state: “Compare the token's number to the number of cards in the triggering player's hand (Action AND Contamination cards both count). Fewer cards than the number → Surprise Attack (an Intruder Attack against that Character). Equal or more → nothing happens.” The Quick Reference likewise says the drawn non-Blank token is kept aside “until a rule returns it, such as an Intruder hiding in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: How Danger resolves when several eligible neighboring Intruders are present.
What happens when no eligible neighboring Intruders are present.
Whether moving an Intruder into the Character's Room through Danger is an Encounter.
How Slime changes a Silence result.
answers.answer: 1. Move all eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into the destination Room; eligible means not in Combat with any Character. 2. If there are no eligible Intruders, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one, including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance. 3. No. An Intruder that merely moves into a Character's Room is not an Encounter; it simply leaves them in Combat. 4. If the Character has a Slime marker, a Silence result is resolved as Danger instead.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Exploration rules state: “Danger — no Movement Noise roll. Move ALL eligible Intruders from neighboring Rooms into this Room (eligible means not in Combat with any Character). If there are none eligible, place a Noise marker in every Corridor connected to this Room that lacks one, counting Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance.” 3. Encounter rules state: “An Intruder merely moving into a Room with a Character is NOT an Encounter (they are simply in Combat).” 4. Exploration rules state: “Silence — no Movement Noise roll. Nothing happens. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.” Noise rules likewise say: “Silence: nothing happens; no marker. If your Character has a Slime marker, resolve "Danger" instead.”

requested_parts: What happens to Noise and the Blank token when an Encounter draws Blank.
When bag development adds an Adult after an Encounter Blank.
How Blank behaves during Intruder bag development.
answers.answer: 1. During an Encounter, a Blank causes a Noise marker to be placed in every Corridor connected to the Room; return the Blank to the bag, and no miniature appears. 2. Add one Adult to the bag only if the Blank was the last token in the bag and an Adult token is available; otherwise add none. 3. During bag development, Blank instead adds one Adult token if any are available, with no last-token condition, then the Blank itself is returned to the bag.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Encounter rules state: “Blank token in an Encounter: place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room. If the Blank was the LAST token in the bag: add 1 Adult token to the bag (if any are available; otherwise nothing). Return the Blank token to the bag. The Encounter ends (no miniature appears).” 3. Intruder bag development says: “Blank — add 1 Adult Intruder token to the bag (if none are available, nothing happens). Return the Blank token to the bag.” Inference: the bag-development rule does not include the Encounter rule's condition that the Blank be the last token in the bag.

requested_parts: Where two Intruders end when attempting to move together through the same Closed Door.
What happens to the Closed Door and whether it may later be closed again.
Whether a Noise-triggered Intruder appearance through a Closed Door is blocked.
answers.answer: 1. Both Intruders remain in the Room they attempted to leave. 2. They destroy the Closed Door simultaneously, leaving its token lying to represent a Destroyed Door. It cannot later be closed by ordinary Door-closing effects; only the Plasma Torch Item can close a Destroyed Door. 3. No. An Intruder appearing through a Corridor as a result of a Noise roll appears regardless of a Closed Door.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Door rules state: “Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws). An Intruder trying to move through a Closed Door does not move — it destroys the Door instead (several Intruders moving from the same Room destroy it simultaneously and all stay put).” They also state: “Destroyed = lying token: movement allowed; only the Plasma Torch Item can Close a Destroyed Door. Other Door-closing effects cannot Close it.” 3. Door rules state: “If a Noise roll causes an Intruder to come through a Corridor with a Closed Door, it appears regardless of the Door.”

requested_parts: What happens to an injured Intruder's miniature, Injury markers and token when it enters Technical Corridors where Noise is already present.
Whether the Noise marker is removed.
Whether Characters and Doors can normally use Technical Corridors.
answers.answer: 1. The Intruder disappears into the ducts: remove its miniature from the board, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the Intruder bag. 2. The Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is not removed. 3. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except through the Mechanic's Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans Item. Door tokens can never be placed there.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Technical Corridors rules state: “If an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, it disappears into the ducts: discard all its Injury markers, return its token to the Intruder bag, and remove its miniature from the board. A Noise marker on the Technical Corridors space is NOT removed by this.” 3. The same section says: “Some Rooms have Technical Corridors Entrances, all linked to the single Technical Corridors space. Characters can never use them (the only exceptions: the Mechanic's "Technical Corridors" Action card and the "Technical Corridor Plans" Item card).” It also states: “Door tokens can never be placed in Technical Corridors.”

requested_parts: Action-card costs for Shoot and Melee.
Shoot's Weapon, Ammo and target requirements.
Melee's Contamination card handling and target requirements.
What happens on a miss for each Action.
How a double-hit result resolves for Shoot versus Melee.
answers.answer: 1. Each is a Basic Action costing 1 Action card. 2. Shoot requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo; choose one Intruder in your Room, discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon, and roll the Combat die. 3. For Melee, draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile, choose an Intruder in your Room, and roll the die. 4. An ordinary Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries and gives the shooter no Wound. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and gives the attacker 1 Serious Wound. 5. A double-hit result normally deals 2 Injuries in Shoot, before Weapon modifiers; in Melee it deals 1 Injury.
answers.evidence: 1. The Basic Actions heading says: “Basic Actions (available to every Character; cost 1 Action card, except Careful Movement which costs 2).” 2–3. Combat rules state: “Shoot (cost 1): requires a Weapon in Hand with at least 1 Ammo. (1) Choose a Weapon and 1 target Intruder in your Room; (2) discard 1 Ammo from the Weapon card; (3) roll the Combat die.” They state: “Melee Attack (cost 1): (1) draw 1 Contamination card and put it on top of your Action discard pile; (2) choose 1 target Intruder in your Room; (3) roll the Combat die.” 4. The summary states: “Ordinary attack misses: a Shoot miss deals 0 Injuries to the target and causes no Wound to the shooter. A Melee miss deals 0 Injuries and causes 1 Serious Wound to the attacker.” 5. Combat table states: “Double-hit symbol | 2 Injuries to any Intruder type before Weapon modifiers | 1 Injury to any Intruder type.”

requested_parts: How Larva death is checked and what happens to it on death.
How Adult death is checked and what happens to it on death.
How Queen death is checked and what happens to it on death.
How a Retreat arrow on the Queen's Injury Effect check changes the outcome.
answers.answer: 1. Compare the Larva's current total Injuries: 1 Injury kills it; remove its miniature and place no Carcass. 2. Draw 1 Intruder Attack card and use its blood value only; if blood is less than or equal to current total Injuries the Adult dies, otherwise it lives. On death remove its miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 3. For a Queen, draw 2 Attack cards and sum their blood values; if the sum is less than or equal to current total Injuries she dies, otherwise she lives. On death remove her miniature and place a Carcass in the Room. 4. If either card drawn for the Queen has the Retreat arrow, she retreats instead of resolving a numerical death/endurance result: draw an Event card, move her via the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card.
answers.evidence: 1–3. Intruder Injuries and death says to compare “current total Injuries, not just the latest hit.” The table states: “Larva | 1 Injury kills | Remove miniature; no Carcass”; “Adult | Draw 1 Intruder Attack card; use only its blood value. Blood ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room”; and “Queen | Draw 2 Attack cards and sum blood values. Sum ≤ Injuries kills; higher means alive. | Remove miniature; place Carcass in Room.” 4. Retreat rules state: “during an Injury Effect check, if any drawn card's blood icon contains the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical endurance/death result. The Intruder flees: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor whose number appears in that card's Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The Queen and Breeders retreat if EITHER of their 2 drawn cards shows the Retreat symbol.”

requested_parts: When Escape attacks resolve and how many occur, including their order.
Who is targeted by the attacks during Escape.
Where the Character's Corpse stays if they die.
What follows if they survive into an empty unexplored destination.
answers.answer: 1. Before moving, resolve one separate Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room; resolve larger Intruders first in this order: Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva. 2. Each Escape attack targets the escaping Character. 3. If the Character dies, their Corpse stays in the Room they tried to Escape from. 4. If they survive, complete the move into the neighboring Room; since it is unexplored, explore it normally, then make a Noise roll because it is empty (unless a Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces that roll).
answers.evidence: 1, 3–4. Character Escape states: “to leave a Room containing Intruders, perform a Movement Action (cost 1) to a neighboring Room (explored or unexplored). BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.” 2. Intruder Attack rules state: “An Escape attack targets the escaper.” The Intruder attack target rule says: “A Surprise Attack targets the Character who triggered the Encounter; an Escape attack targets the escaper.” For unexplored movement, the Movement rules state: “After entering a Room: (1) if the Room tile was unexplored (face down), flip it face up and reveal and resolve its Exploration token, then return that token to the box (removed from the game); (2) apply the Movement Noise rule. A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.” Inference: an empty unexplored destination meets the stated condition for the usual post-move Noise roll, except when exploration replaces it.

requested_parts: How the target is chosen when several Characters are in the Room and how a tie is broken.
How an ordinary Intruder Attack hits or misses.
What changes for a Larva attack.
Where the Contamination card gained from Larva attack is placed.
answers.answer: 1. Target the Character whose player has the fewest Action cards in hand; a tie goes to the Character with the First Player token or the next player in turn order. 2. For an Intruder other than Larva, draw an Intruder Attack card: a matching Intruder-type symbol means resolve its effect; a nonmatching symbol means the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon for attacks, then discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile. 3. A Larva draws no Attack card; instead it is removed from the board and placed on the target's Character board, and that Character gains 1 Contamination card. If they already have a Larva, the attacker disappears, the existing Larva stays, and the Character gains only the Contamination card without automatically dying. 4. A Contamination card is placed on top of that Character's Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Intruder Attack rules state: “Choose the target: the Intruder attacks a Character in its Room — with several Characters present, the one whose player has the FEWEST Action cards in hand; on a tie, the Character with the First Player token (or the next player in turn order).” For non-Larvae: “draw 1 Intruder Attack card: if it shows a symbol matching the attacking Intruder's type, resolve the card's effect; otherwise the attack misses. Ignore the blood icon during attacks. Discard the card to the Intruder Attack discard pile; if the deck runs out, reshuffle the discard pile into a new deck.” 3. Infest says: “A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).” 4. Contamination rules state: “When a Character "gets a Contamination card," draw it from the Contamination deck and place it on top of their Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether dressing one Serious Wound prevents death from a Light Wound when at three Serious Wounds.
What a third Light Wound does otherwise.
What Heal removes.
Where the Corpse and Heavy Objects go upon death.
answers.answer: 1. No. Dressing makes the Serious Wound's effect ignored but it still counts toward the three-wound limit; with 3 Serious Wounds, any additional Light or Serious Wound causes instant death even if one is dressed. 2. On a third Light Wound, clear the Light Wound track and suffer a Serious Wound. 3. Heal removes a Light Wound or discards a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies. 4. On death, remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room, and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: 1–4. Wounds rules state: “Light Wounds: track on your Character board — 1st marker on the upper space, 2nd on the lower space (= 2 Light Wounds); on a 3rd, clear the track and suffer a Serious Wound.” They state: “Death: a Character with 3 Serious Wounds dies instantly upon suffering ANY additional Wound (Light or Serious). Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.” Dressing and healing rules state: “Dress a Serious Wound: flip the card face down — its effect is ignored, but it still counts toward the 3-wound limit. Dressing does not prevent death from a further Wound when you already have 3 Serious Wounds. Heal: remove a Light Wound or discard a Dressed Serious Wound card, as the healing effect specifies.”

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Canteen and Shower scan.
Which scanned cards those Rooms remove and how they handle Infected cards/Larvae.
Which cards Surgery scans and removes and how it handles a Larva.
Surgery's Action cost, wound and passing/shuffle consequences.
answers.answer: 1. Canteen and Shower may scan all Contamination cards in your hand only. 2. They remove all non-Infected scanned cards. An Infected result keeps the card and places a Larva on your Character board; if you already had a Larva, you die and a Creeper appears in the Room. The Canteen also heals 1 Light Wound; Shower removes your Slime marker. 3. Surgery scans all your Contamination cards in your deck, hand and discard pile, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva from your board if present. 4. Surgery is a Room Action costing 2 Action cards; after it, suffer 1 Light Wound, automatically pass, and shuffle all your cards (including your entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: 1–2. Room Actions list Canteen: “Heal 1 Light Wound; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (an Infected result places a Larva on your board — with a Larva already there, you die and a Creeper appears in your Room).” Shower Room: “discard your Slime marker; you may also Scan all Contamination cards in your HAND and remove all non-Infected ones (Infected → Larva, as in the Canteen).” Canteen/Shower scan outcomes state: “Non-Infected | Remove the scanned non-Infected card from the game | No Larva from that result”; “Infected, no Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Place a Larva on Character board”; “Infected, Larva already on board | Keep the Infected card | Character dies; place 1 Creeper in the death Room.” 3–4. Surgery Room Action says: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” Common Room Action requirements say: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.”

requested_parts: How Shoot and Melee destroy uncarried Eggs, including Melee miss exceptions.
How Grenades and Molotov destroy uncarried Eggs.
How Fire destroys Eggs and when the Nest is destroyed.
When and where Noise is rolled for each attack attempt.
answers.answer: 1. Each Injury from Shoot or Melee destroys one uncarried Egg. For Egg Melee, a successful attack still draws one Contamination card to the Action discard pile; a miss causes neither Contamination nor a Wound. 2. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs; Molotov destroys 1 Egg immediately. An uncarried Egg lets its Room be targeted as if an Intruder were there. 3. A Fire marker normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg in each Event Phase Fire Damage step; if the Nest Egg pool has Vulnerability to Fire, it destroys 2 per step. The Nest is destroyed when no Eggs remain, whether carried away or destroyed; mark it with 1 Injury marker. 4. After every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise, including after a miss. For a Grenade/Molotov thrown remotely, roll in your own Room, not in the Nest.

requested_parts: What Hatch Control System changes.

requested_parts: What the Cockpit lets a Character learn or change.
Whether Coordinate information is public or can be misrepresented.

You cannot Set Destination while an Intruder is in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating. The marker selects one of the four destination entries on the Coordinates card: read the entry corresponding to its track space when checking where the ship will jump. You can never Set Destination with an Intruder in the Cockpit, or change Destination once anyone is hibernating.” Combat rule: “Whenever a Character and an Intruder share a Room, they are in Combat.” Room Action rule: “You cannot perform a Room Action while in Combat or in a Room with a Malfunction marker.” Common Room Action rule: “your Character must be in the Room whose Action you use, outside Combat, and the Room must have no Malfunction marker. Pay 2 Action cards.” Inference: an Intruder in the Cockpit prevents use of its Room Actions under the general Combat restriction; the specific rule also separately prohibits setting Destination with an Intruder there.

requested_parts: How Engine checking differs from repairing/breaking.

You do not need to check the Engine first; repair/break works even with a Malfunction marker. Repair/Break Engine (via a Repairs Action or Tools Item): secretly examine both tokens and restack them in any order — you needn't say whether you repaired it, but you MUST say if you changed the order. Works even with a Malfunction marker and without checking first.” Malfunction rules say the Room's Action is unavailable; the Engine rule specifies repair/break via an Action or Item, and explicitly says it works with Malfunction. requested_parts: What occurs when Time reaches its final red space, including Character and Intruder outcomes.

How an active Self-Destruct is resolved at that point.

When the last alive, non-hibernating Character aboard dies, hibernates or launches, the game ends. 3. If Self-Destruct was active, move its marker to its final red space and resolve the explosion; if it was not active, move Time to its final red space and resolve the jump. 4. Intruders do not die from a normal jump; they are unharmed by hyperjump. If Self-Destruct reaches the final skull space, all aboard including Intruders die.

Examples given are locking someone in a burning Room, activating Self-Destruct while people are aboard, and throwing a Grenade into a Room with other crew.

requested_parts: Where a launched Escape Pod passenger is treated as arriving.
Whether that means the ship itself reached Earth.

requested_parts: Whether a Character waiting in a Pod rolls Noise when Adult bag development calls for it.

requested_parts: How many attacks occur when Escaping with multiple Intruders present.

requested_parts: Whether an Event that says to remove itself is removed when its other effect cannot be resolved.
answers.answer: Yes. Remove the Event from the game even if its other effect cannot be resolved.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings state: “Remove an Event that says to remove itself even when its other effect cannot resolve (Rules 6).”

requested_parts: When the Adult token drawn during bag development returns to the bag.
Whether an Encounter triggered by the resulting Noise rolls can draw the same token.
answers.answer: 1. Return the Adult token to the bag immediately before players roll Noise in order, skipping Characters in Combat. 2. Yes. An Encounter from those Noise rolls may draw that same Adult token.
answers.evidence: Adult bag development states: “Adult — return the token to the bag immediately before all players roll for Noise in order (skip Characters in Combat). An Encounter from those rolls may draw that same Adult token (FAQ Rules 7).”

requested_parts: What a retreating Intruder normally does at a Closed Door.
What The Way of Moving Weakness changes for an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen.
answers.answer: 1. Normally, the retreating Intruder destroys the Closed Door and stays in its Room. 2. With The Way of Moving Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings state: “A retreating Intruder meeting a Closed Door destroys it and stays. With The Way of Moving Weakness, an affected Intruder other than a Breeder or Queen instead does nothing at that Door (Rules 8).”

requested_parts: Whether the Hand Serious Wound increases the cost of Basic Shoot.
Why it does or does not.
answers.answer: No. The Hand Serious Wound does not increase the cost of Basic Shoot because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action.
answers.evidence: FAQ Actions and character abilities state: “The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7).”

requested_parts: How much extra Injury Vulnerability to Fire adds per damage instance.
The injury total for a Flamethrower double-crosshair hit under that Weakness.
answers.answer: 1. Vulnerability to Fire adds 1 Injury per damage instance, not per individual Injury. 2. A Flamethrower double-crosshair normally deals 2 Injuries; with the Weakness add 1, for 3 Injuries total.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings state: “Vulnerability to Fire gives 1 additional Injury per damage instance (x + 1), rather than per individual Injury. A Flamethrower double-crosshair hit therefore deals 3 Injuries; Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7).” Inference: the double-crosshair's 2 normal Injuries plus 1 additional Injury per that damage instance equals 3, as the rule explicitly confirms.

requested_parts: What happens to the attacking Larva when its target already has a Larva.
What happens to the existing Larva.
What happens to the Character.
answers.answer: 1. The attacking Larva disappears from the board. 2. The Larva already on the Character board stays. 3. The Character gains 1 Contamination card but is not automatically killed by this attack.
answers.evidence: Infest rules state: “A Larva does not draw Attack cards. Instead: remove the Larva miniature from the board and place it on the target's Character board (on the miniature picture), and the target gains 1 Contamination card. If the target already has a Larva, the attacking Larva disappears, the existing one stays, and the Character only gains the Contamination card; this attack does not automatically kill them (FAQ Rules 12).”

requested_parts: Whether a sleeper takes Fire wounds after Fire appears in the Hibernatorium.
What can still kill a hibernating Character.
answers.answer: 1. No. A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium. 2. Ship destruction and endgame survival checks still matter: ship explosion kills hibernating Characters; a non-Earth destination kills sleepers except a Quarantine Objective sleeper at Mars; and surviving sleepers still face the final Contamination check, which can kill them.
answers.evidence: FAQ says: “A sleeper takes no later Fire wounds in the Hibernatorium, though ship destruction and the endgame survival checks still matter (Rules 13).” Endgame explosion rule states: “the ship explodes / loses hull integrity: ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die.” Coordinates check states: “Non-Earth kills hibernating Characters, while the ship is not destroyed and Intruders remain alive. A sleeper with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars.” Contamination check applies “for every surviving Character, including launched Pod passengers,” and states: “Any Contamination card among those four kills you, whether Infected or not.”

requested_parts: Whether Coolant Leak Event may start Self-Destruct while someone is hibernating.
Whether a Character may start it under the same conditions.
answers.answer: 1. Yes. The Coolant Leak Event can start Self-Destruct even while a Character is hibernating. 2. A Character cannot start Self-Destruct while anyone is hibernating; this Event is the stated exception.
answers.evidence: Self-Destruct rules state: “Characters cannot start Self-Destruct while any Character is hibernating; the Coolant Leak Event can start it despite sleepers (FAQ Rules 14).”

requested_parts: Where discarded/dead Intruder tokens go.
Whether they can be reused.
answers.answer: Discarded or dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool; they are not removed permanently and can be reused later.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings state: “Discarded/dead Intruder tokens return to the unused token pool and remain reusable; they are not removed permanently (Rules 19).”

requested_parts: Whether a Fire marker may be placed in an unexplored Room.
Whether a Malfunction marker may be placed in an unexplored Room.
answers.answer: Fire may be placed in an unexplored Room. Malfunction may not be placed in an unexplored Room.
answers.evidence: Marker rules state: “Malfunction markers cannot be placed in unexplored Rooms, whereas Fire markers can (FAQ Rules 22).”

requested_parts: Which Wounds remain after a Character with 2 Light Wounds suffers 2 more Light Wounds.
answers.answer: After the first new Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes 1 Serious Wound, the second new Light Wound becomes 1 Light Wound. The result is 1 Serious Wound and 1 Light Wound.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings state: “Two Light Wounds suffered while already at 2 Light Wounds become 1 Serious Wound plus 1 remaining Light Wound (Rules 23).” Inference: the first incoming wound is the third Light Wound and triggers the Serious Wound; the second is the remaining Light Wound, matching the explicit result in the rule.

requested_parts: What happens to Heavy Objects when a Character dies in standard play.
What happens to the dead Character's Item cards.
answers.answer: All Heavy Objects drop in the Room where the Character died. The Character's Item cards disappear from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rulings state: “On death in standard play, Heavy Objects drop in the Room, while Item cards disappear from the game (Rules 24).” Wound/death rules also say: “Remove the miniature, place a Character Corpse token in the Room (now a Character Corpse Object), and drop all their Heavy Objects there.”

requested_parts: Whether reaching a later yellow Self-Destruct space unlocks Pods again after they were relocked.
answers.answer: No. Pods unlock automatically only when Self-Destruct first reaches a yellow space. They may be relocked, and subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again.
answers.evidence: Self-Destruct rules state: “At the first yellow space: the sequence can no longer be aborted, and all Escape Pods unlock instantly. They can be re-Locked; subsequent yellow spaces do not unlock them again (FAQ Rules 25).”

requested_parts: Whether ship destruction fulfills kill-the-Queen or destroy-the-Nest Objective requirements.
Whether ship destruction alone makes the Character a winner.
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-the-Queen/destroy-the-Nest requirements. 2. No. Your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective. If aboard when the ship explodes, the Character dies; only a surviving Character can win.
answers.evidence: FAQ says: “Destruction of the ship fulfills kill-Queen/destroy-Nest requirements; your Character must still survive and fulfill their Objective (Rules 26).” Victory rules state a player wins only if they fulfill their Objective and survive. Explosion rules state: “ALL Characters on board (awake and hibernated) die.”

requested_parts: Whether a player may intentionally spend Trade with no intention of exchange.
What happens if genuine negotiations end without a trade.
answers.answer: 1. No. Empty Actions with no meaningful game-state change are disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. 2. Yes. Honest negotiations may end without a trade.
answers.evidence: FAQ Actions state: “Empty Actions that make no meaningful game-state change should be disallowed, including starting Trade with no intention of exchange. Honest negotiations may end with no trade. Any Characters in the Room can trade with each other, including pairs who did not initiate/pay (Actions 1–2).”

requested_parts: What kind of Action activates a Quest Item.
Whether activation is allowed in Combat.
Whether a Room Malfunction prevents activation.
answers.answer: 1. Activating a Quest Item is a Basic Action costing 1 Action card. 2. It is forbidden in Combat. 3. A Room Malfunction does not prevent activation.
answers.evidence: Quest activation ruling states: “Quest activation is a Basic Action printed on its card, forbidden in Combat but allowed in a Malfunctioning Room (Actions 3; Items 10).” The illustrated Quest Items heading says: “Each activation below is a cost-1 Basic Action, out of Combat. It flips the Quest card into its active Item; a Room Malfunction does not prevent this activation.”

requested_parts: Which Basic Actions may be used in Combat.
Whether Trade, Craft or Pick Up Heavy Object are allowed there.
Whether qualifying Action-card or Item Actions may be used in Combat.
answers.answer: 1. The permitted Basic Actions in Combat are Shoot, Melee Attack and Basic Movement as Escape. 2. Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object and Quest Item activation are not permitted; Room Actions are also forbidden. 3. Card or Item Actions may be used when their Combat marking permits it: In Combat Only actions are allowed with an Intruder in your Room, and unmarked actions may be used in either state subject to their own requirements; Out of Combat Only actions remain prohibited.
answers.evidence: Combat limits state: “Basic Actions in Combat are limited to Shoot, Melee and Basic Movement as Escape: no Trade, Craft, Pick Up Heavy Object or Quest Item activation. Room Actions remain forbidden (FAQ Actions 3–5).” Combat marking rules say: “In Combat only | You may use it only while an Intruder is in your Room”; “Out of Combat only | You may use it only while no Intruder is in your Room”; and “No Combat marking on a card or Item Action | You may use it in either situation, subject to its own requirements. Basic and Room Actions retain the separate limits below.”

requested_parts: Whether Soldier may use Covering Fire to move only themselves.
How the two Characters choose movement direction.
How many Noise rolls occur.
Which Character is used for the Surprise Attack comparison.
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Soldier may use Covering Fire for themselves alone. 2. If moving both, each of the two Characters goes in the direction of their choice. 3. Perform one Noise roll after the movement. 4. Any Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier.
answers.evidence: FAQ says: “Covering Fire: Soldier may use it for themselves alone. Both moving Characters go in the direction of their choice, then perform one Noise roll; an Encounter checks Surprise against Soldier (Actions 7).”

requested_parts: How Full Auto spends Ammo.
How it calculates injuries from the Shoot result, spent Ammo and Assault Rifle bonus.
answers.answer: 1. Discard all Ammo from the Assault Rifle, then perform one Shoot Action. 2. Damage equals the Shoot result plus half the discarded Ammo rounded down, plus the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus.
answers.evidence: Full Auto ruling states: “remove all Ammo, perform one Shoot Action; damage adds the Shoot result, half discarded Ammo rounded down, and the Assault Rifle's +1 bonus (Actions 8).” The Action-card description also states that Full Auto discards all Ammo from your Assault Rifle and performs a Shoot Action.

requested_parts: When Soldier may choose Nerves of Steel relative to seeing the Attack card.
Whether it may protect Soldier when another Character triggered the Surprise Attack.
Who receives protection and what happens to other affected Characters.
answers.answer: 1. Soldier may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing Nerves of Steel. 2. Yes, it may protect Soldier even when another Character triggered the Surprise Attack. 3. Only Soldier benefits; other Characters still suffer effects that apply to them, such as Frenzy.
answers.evidence: Nerves of Steel ruling states: “you may see the Intruder Attack card before choosing it. It can protect Soldier when another Character triggered a Surprise Attack, but only Soldier benefits; other Characters still take effects such as Frenzy (Actions 9–10).”

requested_parts: What happens to automatic Danger or Silence Exploration results during Careful Movement.
What happens to those automatic results during Reconnaissance.
What replaces or cancels them.
answers.answer: 1. With Careful Movement, the automatic Silence/Danger result is replaced; use the chosen Noise placement instead of resolving the Exploration result. 2. Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too. 3. Careful Movement places a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination Room; Reconnaissance cancels the automatic result rather than applying that result.
answers.evidence: Careful Movement says: “instead of a Noise roll after moving, place a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the Room you enter.” Its clarification states: “Careful Movement also replaces automatic Silence/Danger Exploration results with its chosen Noise placement; Reconnaissance cancels those automatic results too.” Movement rules state: “A Silence or Danger Exploration result replaces the Movement Noise roll: resolve that result and do not roll Noise again afterward.” The explicit Careful Movement/Reconnaissance FAQ clarification overrides that usual automatic resolution in those cases.

requested_parts: Whether Captain can use Order while Captain is personally in Combat.
Whether Intercom can direct another Character to Move out of Combat.
Which Escape rules apply to that Movement.
answers.answer: 1. No. Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. 2. Intercom may make another Character Move out of Combat. 3. That Character must apply the normal Escape procedure, including an Intruder Attack before moving and the ordinary move/exploration/Noise rules if they survive.
answers.evidence: FAQ says: “Captain cannot use Order while personally in Combat. Intercom may make someone else Move out of Combat, applying normal Escape (Actions 12–13).” Character Escape rules state: “BEFORE moving, resolve an Intruder Attack — one separate Attack per Intruder in the Room, starting with the larger ones (Queen, Breeder, Adult, Larva; FAQ Rules 5). If you survive, complete the move (Noise roll if the destination is empty; explore normally if unexplored). If you die, your Corpse stays in the Room you tried to Escape from.”

requested_parts: Which Characters may draw an Action card when Captain uses Motivation with active Intercom.
answers.answer: All Characters in Rooms with a Computer, as well as all Characters in Captain's Room, are affected and may draw the Action card.
answers.evidence: FAQ states: “Motivation with Intercom affects all Characters in Rooms with a Computer as well as all Characters in Captain's Room (Actions 12–13).”

requested_parts: What happens to a Door Exploration token encountered while entering via the Technical Corridors Action or Plans Item.
Where a Door token is placed in this case.
answers.answer: Ignore the Door Exploration token; do not place a Door token. The Corridor used to enter cannot be determined for Technical Corridors movement.
answers.evidence: FAQ states: “Entering via Technical Corridors Action or Technical Corridor Plans ignores a Door Exploration token because the entry Corridor cannot be determined (Actions 14).”

requested_parts: Whether a Character outside the Captain's Room can Interrupt an Order played remotely through Intercom.
Whether passing prevents a Character from playing Interruption.
answers.answer: 1. No. Interruption requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere. 2. Passing does not by itself prevent Interruption; it remains permitted after passing, subject to the usual card requirements, including the same-Room requirement.
answers.evidence: FAQ says: “Interruption may still be played after passing, but it requires being in the same Room as the Character performing the interrupted Action; a remote Order via Intercom cannot be Interrupted from elsewhere (Rules 21; Actions 17).” The passing rules state: “You may still play Interruption after passing, subject to its usual card requirements (FAQ Rules 21).”

requested_parts: Whether an empty hand automatically causes a pass immediately after two Actions.
What timing consequence Fire or Bleeding may have.
answers.answer: 1. No. Completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends the round but does not automatically pass; apply end-of-round effects, wait for the next round, and declare Pass then. 2. Fire or Bleeding can still apply at a round's end, including the later passing round; Fire is applied at the end of the passing round after Pass is declared.
answers.evidence: FAQ says: “completing 2 Actions with an empty hand ends that round, but does not automatically pass you. Apply the round's end effects, then wait for your next round; declare Pass then. That passing round can incur another Fire or Bleeding effect (Actions 18). Fire applies at the end of your passing round, after you declare Pass.”

requested_parts: Whether multiple Infected cards found by Rest can kill a Character who had no Larva before the Action.
When Rest can be fatal.
answers.answer: 1. No. If there was no Larva before Rest, scanning several Infected cards does not kill the Character; place just 1 Larva. 2. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the Character board before the Action.
answers.evidence: FAQ Actions state: “Rest with no Larva before the Action cannot kill you merely because several scanned cards are Infected: place just 1 Larva. Rest can be fatal if a Larva was already on the board before it (Actions 19).” The general ordinary scan rule also says: “If an ordinary Scan shows INFECTED ... place a Larva miniature on your Character board and do NOT remove that Contamination card. If a Larva is already on your board, your Character dies.”

requested_parts: Where the Noise roll is resolved after throwing a Grenade or Molotov at uncarried Nest Eggs from a neighboring Room.
answers.answer: Roll Noise in the thrower's own Room, not in the Nest. A Noise roll follows each single Egg-destruction attack attempt, including a miss.
answers.evidence: Egg rules state: “after every single Shoot, Melee, Grenade or Molotov attempt to destroy an Egg, perform a Noise roll, including a miss. For a remote Grenade/Molotov, roll in your own Room, not the Nest (FAQ Rooms 2).”

requested_parts: Whether Intranet can reveal a Weakness if the Object is outside the Laboratory while the Scientist carries it.
answers.answer: No. The Object itself must be in the Laboratory for research; the Scientist's location does not replace that requirement. Carrying the Object outside the Laboratory is insufficient to reveal its Weakness.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rooms rulings state: “Intranet research still requires the Object itself in the Laboratory, regardless of Scientist's location. Research means Analyse; the Object is retained, including for Objectives (Rooms 3–4).” Laboratory action specifies an Object present in the Room is Analysed to reveal its corresponding Weakness.

requested_parts: Whether Storage's Room Action can be used repeatedly when its Item Counter is zero.
How Storage's Room Action and ordinary Search differ at zero.
answers.answer: 1. Yes. Storage's Room Action may be used repeatedly at a zero Item Counter, paying the normal Room Action cost and restrictions. 2. The counter limits the ordinary Search Action: in other Rooms each Search lowers it by 1 and at zero that room cannot be searched, except for Scout's Scavenging. Storage's Room Action is separate from that Search Action.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rooms ruling states: “Storage's Room Action works repeatedly even with its Item Counter at zero, paying the normal cost and obeying normal Room restrictions. Its counter limits only the Search Action card (Rooms 6).” Search eligibility states: “In other Rooms, each Search lowers the Item Counter by 1; at 0 the Room cannot be searched (exception: Scout's Scavenging).” Common Room Action requirements require the Character to be in that Room, outside Combat, with no Malfunction, and to pay 2 Action cards.

requested_parts: How many Nest Eggs Fire destroys during each Fire Damage step with Vulnerability to Fire discovered.
answers.answer: It destroys 2 Eggs per Event Phase Fire Damage step while the Nest Egg pool has Vulnerability to Fire (up to the number of Eggs still remaining).
answers.evidence: Egg rules state: “Fire marker | Normally destroys 1 uncarried Egg during every Event Phase Fire Damage step. For the Nest's Egg pool, Vulnerability to Fire increases this to 2 per step (FAQ Rooms 7).” FAQ also states: “Fire in the Nest destroys 2 Eggs per Fire Damage step with this Weakness (Rules 11; Rooms 7).”

requested_parts: Whether an Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest restores the Nest's Egg total for destruction purposes.
answers.answer: No. Once taken from the Intruder board, the Egg is a normal Heavy Object; dropping it back in the Nest does not restore the Nest's Egg total or hit points.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rooms rulings state: “An Egg taken from the Intruder board and dropped back in the Nest is a normal Heavy Object and does not restore the Nest's Egg total/hit points (Rooms 2, 9).” Egg rules also say: “Egg tokens on the Intruder board represent the Eggs in the Nest; taking or destroying Eggs removes them from the Intruder board.”

requested_parts: Who chooses the Action card discarded by each Smoke Grenade target.
Where the discarded card goes.
answers.answer: Each affected player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their own hand. The discarded Action card goes face up to that Character's Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: FAQ Items ruling states: “Smoke Grenade's affected player chooses and discards 1 Action card from their hand (Items 1).” Discard routing says: “place a discarded card face up in the appropriate pile”; the table says: “Used/discarded Action cards | That Character's Action discard pile.”

requested_parts: Whether Medkit may be used on another Character.
Whether Bandages may be used on another Character.
answers.answer: Yes. Both Medkit and Bandages may be used to treat another Character.
answers.evidence: FAQ Items ruling states: “Medkit and Bandages may be used on other Characters (Items 2).”

requested_parts: Whether Energy Charge can directly reload another Character's Weapon.
What procedure permits another Character's Weapon to be recharged.
answers.answer: 1. No. You cannot use Energy Charge directly on another Character's Weapon. 2. Trade them the Energy Charge so they can use it in their own round to fully load one of their own Energy Weapons up to its Ammo capacity; the Item costs 1 Action card and is One Use Only, so it is discarded after use.
answers.evidence: Energy Charge rules state: “Fully load 1 of your own Energy Weapons (up to its Ammo capacity) OR Open or Close 1 Door in a Corridor connected to your Room. The normal prohibition on closing Destroyed Doors applies. To reload someone else's Weapon, Trade the Charge to them first; you cannot use it directly on their Weapon.” The Item table also states: “Energy Charge | 1; One Use Only — discard after use.” FAQ reiterates: “Energy Charge cannot directly reload another Character's Weapon: trade them the Charge so they use it in their own round (Items 3).”

requested_parts: Whether Alcohol's scan of an Infected Contamination card places a Larva.
What happens instead.
answers.answer: 1. No. An Infected card scanned by Alcohol does not place a Larva. 2. Instead, gain a new Contamination card.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rooms and Items states: “Alcohol's Infected scan does not place a Larva; instead gain a new Contamination card (Items 4).”

requested_parts: Whether adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to an already-used or empty Energy Weapon immediately gives extra Ammo.
answers.answer: Yes. Attaching an Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used or empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rooms and Items states: “Adding Extended Magazine or Auto Loader to a used/empty Energy Weapon immediately grants extra Ammo (Items 3, 5–6).”

requested_parts: How much Ammo a newly Crafted Flamethrower starts with compared to a searched Weapon.
answers.answer: A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, not with the 1 Ammo that a Weapon found by Searching starts with.
answers.evidence: FAQ Rooms and Items states: “A newly Crafted Flamethrower starts fully loaded, rather than the one Ammo of a searched Weapon (Items 3, 5–6).” The Weapon Ammo rule separately says: “a Weapon found by Searching starts with 1 Ammo.”

requested_parts: Whether the Hand Serious Wound affects Scout's Motion Scanner.
Why it does or does not.
answers.answer: No. It does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner because Motion Scanner is a unique reaction, not an Item Action.
answers.evidence: FAQ Actions and character abilities states: “The Hand Serious Wound does not increase Basic Shoot cost because Shoot is a Basic Action, not an Item Action. It also does not affect Scout's Motion Scanner, which is a unique reaction rather than an Item Action (Rules 9; Items 7).”

requested_parts: Which Contamination cards Antidote scans.
Which scanned cards Antidote removes and how it handles a Larva.
What new Contamination card is gained.
Which cards are reshuffled and which hand cards may be retained.
What happens to the Character's turn after Antidote.
How Surgery differs in scan scope, removal, Larva, wound, passing, reshuffling and hand retention.
answers.answer: 1. Antidote scans all of your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard. 2. It removes all Infected cards from the game and removes a Larva from your Character board if present. 3. You then gain 1 new Contamination card. 4. Reshuffle that new card with the scanned non-Infected Contamination cards and Action cards, except the cards you retain in hand. 5. Then pass; you may keep hand cards. 6. Surgery also scans all Contamination cards in deck, hand and discard, removes all Infected cards and a Larva if present, but gives no new Contamination card. It then causes 1 Light Wound and an automatic pass; shuffle all your cards, including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards, into your Action deck, leaving your hand empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Antidote ruling states: “scan all your Contamination cards in hand, deck and discard; remove all Infected cards from the game and remove a Larva from your Character board, if present. Gain 1 new Contamination card, and reshuffle that new card with non-Infected scanned Contamination and Action cards, except cards retained in your hand. Then pass; you may keep hand cards.” Surgery Room Action states: “Scan ALL your Contamination cards (deck, hand, discard); remove all Infected ones; remove a Larva from your board if present. Then suffer 1 Light Wound and automatically pass, shuffling all your cards (including the entire hand and remaining Contamination cards) into your Action deck. Your hand stays empty until the next turn.” FAQ comparison states: “Surgery also removes a Larva, but shuffles the entire hand too, gives no new Contamination card and costs 1 Light Wound (Items 9; Rooms 1).”

requested_parts: Where a Slime Exploration effect is placed.
Where a Fire Exploration effect is placed.
Where a Malfunction Exploration effect is placed.
Which Corridor receives a Door Exploration effect.
answers.answer: 1. Place a Slime status marker on your Character board. 2. Place a Fire marker in the Room. 3. Place a Malfunction marker in the Room. 4. Place the Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.
answers.evidence: Exploration effect rules state: “Slime — place a Slime (Status) marker on your Character board.” “Fire — place a Fire marker in this Room.” “Malfunction — place a Malfunction marker in this Room.” “Doors — place a Door token in the Corridor by which you entered.”

requested_parts: How many Injuries each Intruder in a burning Room takes in the Event Phase Fire Damage step.
When Fire Damage resolves relative to Intruder attacks.
Whether the normal Injury Effect check is triggered.
answers.answer: 1. Each Intruder in the burning Room takes 1 Injury. 2. Fire Damage happens after the Intruder Attack step and before the Event card. 3. Yes. Apply Injury markers and immediately perform the Intruder's normal Injury Effect check, including possible death or retreat.
answers.evidence: Event Phase order states: “advance Time/Self-Destruct → Intruder Attacks → Fire Damage → Event card (movement, then effect) → Intruder bag development.” Fire Damage rule says: “each Intruder in a Room with a Fire marker suffers 1 Injury. Apply Injury markers and the normal Injury Effect check immediately (including possible death or retreat). This happens after Intruder Attacks and before the Event card.” Marker rules also state: “each Event Phase, each Intruder in a burning Room suffers 1 Injury and immediately makes its usual Injury Effect check.”

requested_parts: Whether Search Actions are allowed in the Nest.
Whether Search Actions are allowed in Room Covered With Slime.
answers.answer: No. The Nest and Room Covered With Slime prohibit Search Actions.
answers.evidence: Search eligibility states: “The Nest and Room Covered With Slime also prohibit any Search Action, although they are Room tiles rather than those five printed Special Rooms.” Room reference says: “Nest — take 1 Egg token from the Intruder board, then make a Noise roll. No Search Action here.” It also says Room Covered With Slime has “no Search Action.”

requested_parts: Whether a Grenade may be thrown through a Closed Door into an Intruder's neighboring Room.
answers.answer: No. A Closed Door blocks Grenade throws, even when the target Room is neighboring and contains an Intruder.
answers.evidence: Door rules state: “Closed = standing token: blocks Character and Intruder movement (and Grenade throws).”
